title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: Foreign affairs budget cut debate
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce Head N of the Estimates by $100, opening debate on international affairs and MFA's views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head N of the Estimates be reduced by $100." As in previous years, I would like to kick off the debate with a broad overview of developments in international affairs and ask the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) for its views on their potential implications for Singapore.

sections.label: Belt and Road initiative role
sections.summary: The Belt and Road initiative continues to play a growing role in regional and global development, supporting infrastructure investments and big projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Belt and Road (B&R) initiative continues to play a growing role in regional and global development, supporting infrastructure investments and big projects.

sections.label: US withdrawal and North Korea
sections.summary: US exits from the Paris Agreement and TPP suggest it is more inward-looking, while North Korea's nuclear issue remains despite eased Korean tensions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The US' decisions to pull out of key multilateral deals, like the Paris Agreement on Climate Change and the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), also support this concern that the US is becoming more inward-looking and less interested in taking the lead on global issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Barely a few months ago, the North was escalating its nuclear testing and boasting that it was getting close to having a nuclear weapon and intercontinental ballistic capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It appears that the two Koreas are trying to ease tensions at the moment, which is to be welcomed, but the underlying issue of nuclearisation of North Korea remains.

sections.label: MFA on Singapore's challenges
sections.summary: A question asks what MFA sees as the major challenges facing Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What does MFA see as the major challenges facing Singapore?

sections.label: ASEAN Economic Community potential
sections.summary: The ASEAN Economic Community could become an economic powerhouse if the 10 countries establish a single market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Economic Community could also emerge as an economic powerhouse if the 10 countries could garner the political will to establish a single market.

sections.label: Trump exits Trans-Pacific Partnership
sections.summary: In January 2017, President Donald Trump signed an executive order pulling the US out of the TPP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In January 2017, a newly elected President Donald Trump signed an executive order pulling his country out of the TPP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It would have been an ambitious trade deal that would account for 40% of global economic output and 26% of world trade.

sections.label: RCEP and ASEAN economic integration
sections.summary: Singapore as Chairman aims for a high quality RCEP involving all 10 ASEAN member states and six FTA partner countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Singapore, as Chairman, will also aim to achieve a high quality Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), a trade pact involving all 10 ASEAN member states and six countries which ASEAN has Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What is MFA's view on the ability of ASEAN to achieve real economic integration regionally versus bilateral trade agreements with the major economies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As a small and open economy with foreign trade more than three times its gross domestic product (GDP), Singapore is particularly vulnerable to global economic shifts.

sections.label: Cooperation with Central and Eastern Europe
sections.summary: There is scope to explore greater cooperation with Central and Eastern Europe, Russia and Turkey, and the Singapore-Turkey FTA came into force last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Beyond our traditional economic partners in the EU, there is scope to explore greater cooperation with promising markets in Central and Eastern Europe as well as Russia and Turkey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I know that the Singapore-Turkey FTA came into force last year.

sections.label: G20 visit and South Asia markets
sections.summary: The Prime Minister will visit Argentina for the G20 Summit, and Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have good economic growth potentials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister will also be visiting Argentina later this year for the Group of 20 (G20) Summit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In South Asia, apart from India where we already have a strong economic presence, countries like Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have good economic growth potentials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We have an FTA with Sri Lanka, and the Bangladesh Prime Minister is visiting Singapore.

sections.label: Strengthening ASEAN economic integration
sections.summary: Strengthening economic integration is important to tap a market of over 600 million people with a growing middle class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: To maintain ASEAN’s relevance and value, it will be important that we continue to strengthen the economic integration to tap the potential of a market of over 600 million people with a rapidly growing middle class.

sections.label: Model ASEAN Extradition Treaty
sections.summary: Singapore would pursue the Model ASEAN Extradition Treaty under its Chairmanship, among a variety of issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition to a variety of issues that Singapore would be pursuing under its Chairmanship, is the Model ASEAN Extradition Treaty.

sections.label: Model Extradition Treaty timeline and trade
sections.summary: Singapore's chairmanship offers an opportunity to push for an early agreement on the Model Extradition Treaty, and ASEAN committed to doubling intra-ASEAN trade between 2017 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore’s chairmanship of ASEAN this year presents a signature opportunity for MFA to showcase strong thought leadership to push for an early agreement on the Model Extradition treaty that would support the rule of law within ASEAN and catalyse the signing of bilateral extradition treaties between neighbouring countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the Minister have any preliminary timeline with regard to discussions on the Model Extradition Treaty?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: ASEAN has also committed to the ambitious objective under the aegis of the ASEAN Economic Community of doubling intra-ASEAN trade between 2017 and 2025.

sections.label: Singaporean interest in ASEAN news
sections.summary: One survey found only 13% of Singaporean respondents indicated interest in ASEAN news and information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to one of these surveys, only 13% of Singaporean respondents indicated an interest in ASEAN news and information.

sections.label: Rohingya refugees fleeing Rakhine state
sections.summary: Since August 2017, over 688,800 Rohingyas fled Rakhine state, expanding refugee camps beyond capacity without adequate water or sanitation, about 60% children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Excluding those internally displaced who fled in earlier incidents of violence, since August 2017, more than 688,800 Rohingyas have fled the Rakhine state, exponentially expanding refugee camps beyond their capacity, and without adequate water or sanitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Of these, about 60% are children, of whom some have suffered separation, being orphaned or even being raped.

sections.label: Singapore-China investment and trade ties
sections.summary: Singapore has been China's largest foreign investor since 2013 and was the first Asian country to sign a comprehensive FTA with China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore is China's largest foreign investor since 2013 and one of China’s top trading partners in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore was also the first Asian country to sign a comprehensive FTA with China which paved the way for the subsequent ASEAN-China FTA.

sections.label: US-Singapore foreign direct investment
sections.summary: In 2016, the US was Singapore's largest source of FDIs, while Singapore was the US' second largest Asian investor after Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In 2016, the US was Singapore's largest source of foreign direct investments (FDIs), while Singapore was the US' second largest Asian investor after Japan.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia Second Link tolls
sections.summary: Singapore and Malaysia have jointly lowered tolls on the Second Link.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Most recently, Singapore and Malaysia have jointly lowered tolls on the Second Link.

sections.label: Brunei currency agreement and Pedra Branca
sections.summary: Close ties are underscored by the Currency Interchangeability Agreement with Brunei, and Malaysia sought revision of the 2008 ICJ Judgment on Pedra Branca, Middle Rocks and South Ledge.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our close ties are underscored by our special Currency Interchangeability Agreement with Brunei.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One example is how the Malaysians have sought revision and interpretation of the 2008 International Court of Justice (ICJ) Judgment on sovereignty over Pedra Branca, Middle Rocks and South Ledge.

sections.label: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership signing
sections.summary: The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership signed in 2015 upgraded ties across multiple sectors and deepened relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our relations have deepened over the past few years with the signing of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) in 2015, representing a significant upgrade of ties across multiple sectors.

sections.label: Singaporeans studying and visiting Australia
sections.summary: Australian universities remain popular for Singapore tertiary students, and about 400,000 Singaporeans visit Australia yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Australian universities remain to this day a favourite for our tertiary students, and roughly 400,000 Singaporeans visit Australia annually.

sections.label: Forbes report on India projections
sections.summary: A Forbes article reported World Bank and IMF projections that India would be the fastest growing large economy and soon fifth largest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In a Forbes' article dated 10 January 2018, it was reported that World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projected India to be the world's fastest growing large economy for the rest of this decade as well as the world's fifth largest economy soon.

sections.label: Singapore vote on US decision
sections.summary: Singapore supports a two-state solution and voted among 128 UN Member States to reject the US decision at the UN General Assembly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: Singapore has always supported a two-state solution and we are one of the 128 United Nations (UN) Member States that voted in favour of rejecting the US' decision tabled at the United Nations (UN) General Assembly recently.

sections.label: New collaboration areas and Arctic Council
sections.summary: New areas like technology and innovation are being explored, and Singapore is an observer in the Arctic Council given Arctic shipping's importance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And besides traditional areas of collaboration, are there new areas, such as technology and innovation, which we are exploring?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, given the rising importance of the Arctic shipping route, Singapore has strategically placed itself as an observer within the Arctic Council.

sections.label: Millennials' climate concern and Rohingya camps
sections.summary: A 2017 World Economic Forum poll found climate change was millennials' top concern, and the speaker visited Rohingya refugee camps in Bangladesh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A 2017 World Economic Forum poll involving 30,000 millennials from 186 countries found that climate change was their top concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I visited the Rohingya refugee camps in Bangladesh last month, and what I saw and heard were painful and beyond words.

sections.label: Singapore ASEAN chairmanship resilience focus
sections.summary: Singapore chairs ASEAN this year and focuses on strengthening the collective resilience of ASEAN members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Singapore assumes the Chairmanship of ASEAN this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: One of the focuses of our chairmanship year is to strengthen the collective resilience of ASEAN members.

sections.label: ASEAN collective strength and China
sections.summary: Working together leverages a region of over 600 million people and combined GDP over US$2 trillion, while China's rise draws attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Working together allows us to leverage our collective strength as a region of over 600 million people with a combined GDP of over US$2 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: With the rise of China projected to become the world’s largest economy by 2032, it is understandable that the developments there have occupied most of our attention.

sections.label: Singapore hosting ASEAN 2018 meetings
sections.summary: As 2018 ASEAN Chair, Singapore takes on more responsibilities and hosts member states and partners at high-level meetings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: As Chair of ASEAN in 2018 this year, Singapore will have to take on more responsibilities, playing host to the ASEAN member states and key partners at many high-level meetings in Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore human capital and SCP
sections.summary: Singapore ranked top in Asia for human capital and shares development experience through the Singapore Cooperation Programme with partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, the World Economic Forum ranked Singapore top in Asia for developing human capital.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Globally, we were ranked 11th out of 130 countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We are now in a good position to help others by sharing our development experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that our main conduit of assistance has been through the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP), and we have worked with various partners to deliver training programmes for developing countries.

sections.label: Bali travel and MFA assistance
sections.summary: Singaporeans could not travel to Bali after Mount Agung's eruption, prompting a question on MFA measures to assist Singaporeans overseas.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans who had made travel plans to Bali last December were unable to proceed due to Mount Agung's eruption.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In view of the potential dangers that Singaporeans may face overseas, what are some of the measures that MFA has taken or is planning to take to assist Singaporeans in such circumstances?

sections.label: Major powers and ASEAN unity
sections.summary: Questions cover managing relations with major powers and, as ASEAN Chairman, strengthening ASEAN's unity, centrality, identity and sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: First, how do we manage our relations with the major powers, given the rapidly evolving geopolitical balance of power?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The second set of issues is, as ASEAN Chairman, how do we strengthen ASEAN’s unity, centrality and value proposition, and value proposition not just for outsiders but including our own people?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: How do we protect our unique identity, our domestic unity and our sovereignty from the inevitable foreign influence and, especially from the primordial pulls of ancestry, race, language and religion?

sections.label: Singapore foreign policy principles
sections.summary: Singapore's foreign policy has always been guided by five key principles given its unique position.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore’s foreign policy, given our unique position, has always been guided by five key principles.

sections.label: Xi Jinping on Singapore China
sections.summary: President Xi Jinping told the Prime Minister that Singapore and China had no fundamental disagreements, conflicting interests or differences on basic principles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: When the Prime Minister met President Xi Jinping, President Xi emphasised that Singapore and China had no fundamental disagreements, no conflicting interests and no differences on basic principles.

sections.label: Singapore largest investor in China
sections.summary: Singapore has been the largest foreign investor in China since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In fact, surprisingly, Singapore has been the largest foreign investor in China since 2013.

sections.label: China-Singapore FTA upgrade talks
sections.summary: Singapore and China are currently negotiating an upgrade to the China-Singapore FTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Currently, we are negotiating an upgrade to the China-Singapore FTA.

sections.label: Singapore share of B&R investment
sections.summary: Singapore accounted for 85% of total inbound investments to China from B&R countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore accounted for 85% of total inbound investments to China from B&R countries.

sections.label: US investment in Singapore 2016

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In 2016, the US was the top foreign direct investor in Singapore, with investment stock worth S$281 billion.

sections.label: US exports support American jobs
sections.summary: US exports to Singapore and Singapore investments in the US support over 250,000 American jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: US exports to Singapore and Singapore investments in the US support over 250,000 American jobs.

sections.label: Trump accepts Lee's invitation
sections.summary: President Trump has accepted Prime Minister Lee's invitation to visit Singapore later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: President Trump has accepted Prime Minister Lee's invitation to visit Singapore later this year.

sections.label: US GDP share of global GDP
sections.summary: In 2017, although US GDP grew, as a proportion it shrank to 25% of global GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In 2017, although the US GDP has grown, as a proportion, it has shrunk to 25% of the global GDP.

sections.label: Hope for stable US-China relationship
sections.summary: Singapore hopes for a stable US-China relationship because peace between them brings peace, stability and prosperity to the Asia Pacific.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For us, because of our close relationship with both the US and China, clearly, we hope that there will be a stable US-China relationship because, if they maintain the peace, there will be peace, stability and prosperity in the Asia Pacific.

sections.label: Concern over trade war tariffs
sections.summary: Singapore views a trade war with great concern, citing early salvos such as US tariffs on solar panels and washing machines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We, of course, view a trade war with great concern.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have seen some early salvos, for instance, the tariffs that the US is imposing on solar panels, even washing machines.

sections.label: UNCLOS and international law order
sections.summary: Singapore asks whether an initiative supports a world order based on international law, and calls UNCLOS sacrosanct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Third question: whatever the initiative, does it support a world order based on international law?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And for us, in particular, because we are a port, an island, a city-state, the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) is sacrosanct.

sections.label: Chairmanship themes resilience innovation
sections.summary: The Chairmanship themes for this year are resilience and innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our Chairmanship themes for this year are “resilience” and “innovation”.

sections.label: ASEAN Smart Cities Network
sections.summary: One key initiative is the ASEAN Smart Cities Network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: One key initiative is the ASEAN Smart Cities Network.

sections.label: AHA Centre Myanmar relief supplies
sections.summary: The AHA Centre has delivered at least two loads of relief supplies worth US$500,000 to the Myanmar government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: To date, the AHA Centre has delivered at least two loads of relief supplies worth US$500,000 to the Myanmar government.

sections.label: Code of Conduct negotiations
sections.summary: ASEAN and China will commence negotiations on the Code of Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: ASEAN and China will also commence negotiations on the Code of Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea this year.

sections.label: Restructuring economies plan measures
sections.summary: The plan had 609 measures and 536 have been implemented, covering restructuring, skills, innovation and global business opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We believe we have to double down on restructuring our economies, upgrading the skills of our people, supporting innovation and pursuing business opportunities globally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I have been told that, so far, that plan had 609 measures and 536 of them have been implemented.

sections.label: CPTPP signing eleven parties
sections.summary: The 11 remaining TPP parties concluded talks and Minister Lim Hng Kiang will sign the CPTPP in Chile on 8 March.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, the 11 remaining parties of the TPP have concluded talks and, on 8 March, in Chile, Minister Lim Hng Kiang will have to make a long journey to sign the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for TPP (CPTPP).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: However, even with just 11 members because the US has pulled out, it still represents about 500 million people, and a $10 trillion-dollar economy collectively.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat outcomes
sections.summary: At the 8th Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat, the two Prime Ministers opened Marina One and DUO and signed the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link Bilateral Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: At the 8th Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat in January, Prime Minister Lee and Prime Minister Najib Razak officiated the opening of the Marina One and DUO joint venture developments, which have a combined Gross Development Value of S$11 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Members will remember that these projects came about as sequelae to the settlement of the Points of Agreement on the Malaysian Railways (KTM) land.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also signed the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link Bilateral Agreement.

sections.label: Singapore top investor in Indonesia
sections.summary: Singapore remained Indonesia's top foreign investor in 2017, with realised investments at US$8.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore remained Indonesia's top foreign investor in 2017, with realised investments at US$8.4 billion.

sections.label: Haze cooperation with Indonesia
sections.summary: Singapore appreciates efforts by President Joko Widodo and provincial leaders to manage the haze and is committed to working with Indonesia on this transboundary issue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And since I used to be the Environment Minister, I need to say that we appreciate the concerted efforts of President Joko Widodo and the provincial leaders to manage the haze situation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are committed to working with Indonesia to tackle this transboundary issue.

sections.label: Currency Interchangeability Agreement anniversary
sections.summary: The 50th Anniversary of the Currency Interchangeability Agreement was celebrated in July 2017 during the Sultan's fourth State Visit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We want Malaysia and Indonesia especially to succeed – good for us, good for the region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We celebrated the 50th Anniversary of the Currency Interchangeability Agreement (CIA) in July 2017, during the fourth State Visit of His Majesty the Sultan.

sections.label: Singapore-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
sections.summary: Singapore elevated ties with Australia to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2015, and implementation is well on track.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our close friendship with Australia is underpinned by shared historical experiences and shared strategic perspectives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We elevated our ties with Australia to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2015, and implementation is well on track.

sections.label: UNSC resolutions and Korean Peninsula
sections.summary: Singapore has implemented UNSC Resolutions fully and hopes recent ROK-DPRK talks lead to a peaceful resolution and denuclearisation of the Korean Peninsula.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore has been implementing the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Resolutions fully and faithfully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We hope that the recent talks between the Republic of Korea (ROK) and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) will help them arrive at a peaceful resolution and, ultimately, we hope that there will be a denuclearisation of the Korean Peninsula.

sections.label: MFA outreach to Singaporeans
sections.summary: MFA has been stepping up its outreach to Singaporeans at various levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: On this front, MFA has been stepping up its outreach to Singaporeans at various levels.

sections.label: MFA selection and nurturing officers
sections.summary: MFA has worked on rigorous selection and nurturing systems, training officers who are motivated by advancing Singapore's interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Over the years, MFA has worked on a rigorous selection system and an equally rigorous nurturing system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is up to us to optimise our limited resources to provide our officers with continuous training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But I think, most of all, what really motivates our officers is that sense of meaning and significance that they are advancing Singapore's interests, protecting sovereignty, expanding opportunities for businesses, looking after Singaporeans who get into trouble.

sections.label: Quiet friendly firm diplomacy
sections.summary: Singapore will continue a quiet, friendly but firm style of diplomacy resting on domestic consensus on national interests.

sentences.text: In terms of style, we will continue to adopt a quiet, friendly but firm style of diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our foreign policy rests on a domestic consensus on our national interests.

sections.label: ASEAN trade and visitor figures

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)

sentences.text: We see tremendous potential and opportunities in our region as ASEAN is expected to become the fourth largest economy in the world with a GDP of US$10 trillion by 2030.

sentences.text: For example, Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements with Laos and Cambodia came into force last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)

sections.label: Fake news, North Korea nuclear concerns
sections.summary: A Member asks about fake news from foreign state actors, and the Minister discusses North Korea, UNSC Resolutions and Northeast Asia nuclear deterrence before an amendment is withdrawn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Is there any concern that the Minister has about fake news, say, from foreign state actors or players that we may have to be concerned about?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: There is a North Korean embassy in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: North Korea also attends our ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) meeting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But our approach, as I have explained earlier, is to just fully comply with UNSC Resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: If North Korea effectively nuclearises, quite apart from the dynamics with the US, the other consequential effects are what it means for South Korea and Japan, and whether they will also take the view that they need to have their own deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Again, to use the Cold War analogy, when you have two superpowers working on deterrence based on mutually assured destruction, well, we survived.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But can you imagine a Northeast Asia, which, as Mr Low Thia Khiang will know, unfortunately, historical wounds not fully healed, and all of them nuclear-armed and all promising mutually assured destruction, I think it is a very dangerous situation.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: If there are no other clarifications, can I invite the Member Mr Vikram Nair to consider withdrawing the amendment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I seek leave to withdraw my amendment, Mr Chairman.
